prompt: pulse-bus is our in-process event bus, and after a release last week some handlers fire on topics they never asked for. A worker that subscribes to `user.*` now runs on `user.profile.updated` events, and one that subscribes to `*` receives multi-segment topics. The docs in `docs/events.md` say what the patterns are supposed to mean, so please make the matcher and the emitter agree with them, and keep the existing subscription, ordering and metrics behavior intact. Add or adjust tests as you see fit, but the behavior has to be right for every pattern shape we document, not just the two cases I mentioned.

The billing CSV export comes back with quoted cells mangled. A value like `"""quoted"""` loses its quotes, and `"  padded  "` comes back trimmed even though the quotes are there to keep the spacing, and cells that contain a quote break when we write the table back out with `stringifyCsv`. Please make reading and writing agree with the field rules in `docs/csv.md`, so that writing a table and reading it again gives me the same rows, while plain unquoted cells keep the trimming we rely on today. Add whatever tests you need.

Our cache is supposed to take a `Clock` so tests can control time, but TTLs do not follow it. A test that advances an injected clock past the TTL still gets a hit, `ttl(key)` keeps reporting the full lifetime, and an entry written with `ttl: 0` survives its first read. Please make expiry, remaining TTL, size, `has`, `sweep` and the stats counters all agree with the clock the cache was built with, keeping today's behavior when the system clock is used.

Our retry helper is making one attempt fewer than the policy says, so a job with `maxAttempts: 3` only gets called twice, and the waits it does make can go over `maxDelayMs` once jitter is added. `docs/retries.md` describes what we promised: the total attempt count, the capped wait, and no sleep after the last attempt. Please make `retry` and `computeDelay` follow it, keeping the exponential growth, the `shouldRetry` early exit and the `RetryError` you get when everything fails.

Requests to `/files/:name` come back 404 whenever the name contains an encoded slash, for example `/files/a%2Fb`, because the path normalizer seems to decode the whole path before it splits it. I need the encoded character to stay inside its own segment, while plain multi-segment paths keep behaving as they do now, and `..`, null bytes and broken percent escapes still answer 400 instead of crashing. Keep the middleware, the admin guard and the rest of the routes working, keep `normalizePath` in `src/path.ts` returning the normalized path string (other code calls it), and add tests for whatever you change.

runlog is fine for adding and listing runs, but I keep computing summaries by hand. Please add a `stats` command: it should print `total`, `ok`, `failed`, `skipped`, the average duration in whole milliseconds rounded to the nearest millisecond, and the slowest run as `task (durationMs)`. With `--json` it should print one JSON object instead, with the keys `total`, `ok`, `failed`, `skipped`, `avgDurationMs`, and `slowest` being `{ task, durationMs }` or `null` when the log is empty. An empty or missing log should still exit 0 with zeros and `slowest: none` in the text form, and `help` should mention the new command.

hookrelay forwards inbound partner webhooks straight to the queue, without checking who sent them. We agreed on an `x-relay-signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>` header where the hex is the HMAC-SHA256 of `<t>.<raw body>` with our secret, and a request is stale when `t` is more than `toleranceSeconds` away from our clock in either direction. Please verify the header before anything is enqueued: 400 with `{ "error": "malformed_signature" }` when we cannot parse it, 401 with `{ "error": "timestamp_out_of_range" }` for a stale timestamp, 401 with `{ "error": "bad_signature" }` for a wrong signature, and keep the 202 for a good one. Put the check in `src/webhook/verify.ts` so it can be tested on its own, and make sure a rejected request never reaches the queue.

The admin user list only ever returns the first page, so the UI cannot go further than `limit` users. Please add cursor pagination to `listUsers` and the HTTP layer: `nextCursor` in the response, `cursor` accepted on the next request, a stable order of `createdAt` then `id`, the same 1..100 limit rules and default of 20, and `InvalidCursorError` (mapped to `400 { "error": "invalid_cursor" }`) for anything that is not a cursor this service produced. `docs/api.md` has the contract we published, and the last page must report `nextCursor: null`.

gate-service has auth but no request limit, and one noisy client can still take the whole gate. Please add a sliding-window rate limiter middleware, run after auth, keyed by client IP plus method and path, with the limit and window coming from the config or `createApp({ rateLimit })`. A blocked request must answer `429` with `{ "error": "rate_limited", "retryAfterMs }` where `retryAfterMs` is how long until the oldest counted request leaves the window, plus a `retry-after` header carrying those milliseconds in whole seconds rounded up. Only accepted requests count, a request leaves the window once `windowMs` has passed since it, and the existing auth, logging and route behavior must stay as it is.

We are standardising on the word "settings" for the configuration layer, and `config` is now taken by another service. Please rename `src/config/` to `src/settings/`, and rename the exported API with it: `Config` to `Settings`, `loadConfig` to `loadSettings`, `defaultConfig` to `defaultSettings` and `ConfigSource` to `SettingsSource`, keeping `LoadConfigOptions` as `LoadSettingsOptions`. Update every import and test, delete the old folder, and leave no reference to the old names in `src/` or `test/`; the `App` it builds exposes `settings` instead of `config`, and `AppOptions` takes `settings`. Behavior must stay exactly the same, including the defaults, the merge order and the env keys.

Both services read and write their JSON files by hand and the two versions have drifted, which is how we ended up with a half-written `projects.json` last week. Please add `src/storage/json-store.ts` with `readJson(path, fallback)` (the fallback when the file is missing or does not parse) and `writeJson(path, value)` (creates the directory, writes a temp file in the same directory, then renames it into place), and move both services onto them. Nothing else should change: an empty name or note body still throws, a missing or corrupt file still reads as empty, and two services writing at once must never leave invalid JSON or stray temp files.

We are moving away from the old `http` naming before the next release: `HttpClient` becomes `ApiClient`, `fetchJson` becomes `requestJson`, `HttpError` becomes `ApiError`, and the folder `src/http/` becomes `src/client/`. Please update every import, the barrel in `src/index.ts`, the tests and the docs so nothing in `src/` or `test/` mentions the old names, and keep the behavior identical, including the base-url join, the bearer token, the JSON body handling and the `status`/`payload` on the error.

I need to know what a staging deploy will actually listen on before we cut the release. It will run with `CONF_PROFILE=staging`, the `conf.json` in this repo, `CONF_HTTP_PORT=7000` in the environment and `--port=6000` on the command line. Write `ANSWER.md` in the repo root with exactly these lines: `port: <the effective http.port>`, `overlay: <file>:<the function that applies the profile overlay>`, `list_merge: <file>:<the function that merges list values>`, `sources: <how many sources src/sources/index.ts registers>`, `overlay_disable_env: <the environment variable that turns the overlay off>` and `schema_keys: <how many keys src/schema.ts declares>`. Use paths relative to the repo root, do not change any code, and keep the answer to those six lines.

RSS on the service climbs steadily over a long run and never comes back down, and I suspect one of the two caches. One of them is bounded and one is not, but I need the exact owner before we change anything. Write `ANSWER.md` in the repo root with exactly these lines: `owner: <the file with the unbounded cache>`, `function: <the exported function that stores into it>`, `lru_limit: <the default entry limit of the bounded cache>`, `unbounded_call_sites: <how many places in src/ call the unbounded store>`. Use paths relative to the repo root, change no code, and keep it to those four lines.

In production the orders and cart endpoints always answer `{ "error": "api_not_found" }` while the catalog works, and I cannot see why from the handler code. Something registered earlier is answering for them. Write `ANSWER.md` in the repo root with exactly these lines: `shadow_route: <the method and pattern that swallows them>`, `shadow_file: <file>:<function that registers it>`, `unreachable: <how many registered handlers can never run>`, `orders_file: <the file that defines the order routes>`. Use paths relative to the repo root, change no code, and keep it to those four lines.
